newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks up on overseas gains, rate hope.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks up on overseas gains, rate hope.

text.p: The Australian share market ended 0.55 pct higher on Friday, supported by overseas gains and general expectations of an official interest rate cut in the next few weeks.
The All Ordinaries index rose 14.8 points to 2,691.2.

There was some initial disappointment as the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) failed to deliver a rate cut Friday morning, but investors soon turned their hopes to the RBA's next meeting on August 5. "Everybody expects a cut then," one dealer said.
Dealers said the underlying sentiment remained firm, and that share prices were likely to continue higher next week.
"There is a lot of money coming in from overseas. Our market is seen to be cheap by comparison," Kevin Lourey of Peake Lands Kirwan in Melbourne said.
Turnover amounted to A$1.35 billion (US$999 million), boosted by July series options exercises after Thursday's expiry.
The banking sector received a lot of attention, but performances were mixed and the index only gained a moderate 0.35 percent.

Westpac Banking closed 10 cents up at A$8.23 after hitting a record A$8.24, and Bank of Melbourne rose 14.2 cents to A$9.80 on news that Westpac's bid for the regional bank had received approval by the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) and the Reserve Bank.
National Australia Bank recovered 23 cents of the 45 cents it lost on Thursday following its lower than expected June quarter earnings, and the stock ended the week at A$19.28.
"If you have a look at the figures NAB put out, they were seemingly low. But they increased their provisions for bad debts and that might have been a safety reserve," Kevin Lourey said.

Commonwealth Bank of Australia dipped 25 another cents to A$16.47 in fairly active trade. The bank said on Friday some of its branches could be closed on Monday due to planned industrial action by the Finance Sector Union (FSU), but dealers said the market was more concerned with the bank's earnings.

Among other blue chips, The Broken Hill Pty Ltd, ended 12 cents higher at an even A$18 and WMC closed 15 cents up at A$7.74. Rio Tinto recovered from early losses after weakness in London and ended unchanged at A$21.25.
MIM Holdings led the turnover table with 18.86 million shares traded. It rose one cent to A$1.79.
"There's just been some portfolio movements," one dealer said, adding there were no market moving news on the miner.
Oil Search jumped 13 cents to A$3.87 in fairly high volume of 5.88 million shares.

"There is an increasing realisation that they're sitting on a huge reservoir of oil and looking ahead, maybe five to ten years, I think we'll see a real bonanza in the Oil Search area. The big portfolios are buying," one broker said.
After the market close, the company said it had applied for a license to explore north of the major Moran oil find in Papua New Guinea.
